title: Agent wastes calls learning what exists: where should that knowledge live?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Agent explores to learn a catalogue, hierarchy or schema
Readable content, kept current by the server
The structure is small and rarely changes
Describe it in the system prompt
Static facts can be stated once
Agent must find specific items by query
A search tool with a clear description
Discovery is unavoidable and very verbose
Delegate to a subagent that returns a summary
Agent prefers a built-in over a better MCP tool
rule: If an agent spends tool calls learning what exists, publish that as an MCP resource. Tools are for actions, resources are for content.

title: Where does this MCP server belong?
head: Who needs it
Where
Secret handling
rows: Everyone on the team, from first clone
${VAR} expansion; each person sets the variable
Instructions on how to use a server
A token written into a committed file
rule: Team servers go in the project .mcp.json with ${VAR} tokens; personal or experimental servers go in ~/.claude.json.

title: Claude picks the wrong tool: where is the fix?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Better MCP tool ignored; its description is vague
Rewrite: capabilities, inputs, examples, when to prefer
Several similar tools confused with each other
Rename and split into purpose-specific tools
Misroutes follow specific words in requests
You can't edit a third-party tool's description
A tool must never be used here
rule: Descriptions drive tool choice. If a more capable MCP tool loses to a built-in, describe what it does that the built-in can't.

title: Connecting Claude to a system: reuse or build?
head: Situation
Right choice
Why
rows: Standard system with maintained community servers
rule: Prefer community MCP servers for standard integrations; put team conventions in CLAUDE.md; build custom only when nothing exists.

title: Agent ignores a better tool: what is the cheapest reliable fix?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Better MCP tool ignored; description is thin
Describe its strengths, sample queries, when to prefer it
Competing tool has no legitimate use for this agent
Remove it from the agent's tools
Many exploratory calls just to find content
One generic tool does several jobs
rule: If an agent ignores a better MCP tool, fix its description before removing the alternatives.

title: Where does an MCP server's config live?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Per-person tokens, not a shared one
rule: Commit the shared server definition; keep each person's secret in their environment through ${VAR} expansion.

title: MCP tool not used: missing or ignored?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Claude says it has no such tool; server added mid-session
Tools listed but Claude picks a built-in
Server fails for one person only
rule: Tool missing after a mid-session config change means reconnect; tool present but ignored means improve its description.

title: The agent makes too many calls: is it lost, or is the tool unclear?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Calls are exploratory: probing to learn what content exists
Expose the index as an MCP resource
Calls are badly formed or return irrelevant results
Expand the description: inputs, examples, edge cases
Results are huge and fill the context
Verbose searching pollutes the main conversation
Delegate to a subagent that returns a summary
Agent prefers built-in Grep over a better MCP tool
rule: If the agent is calling tools to find out what exists, give it a catalogue (a resource). Better descriptions fix badly formed calls.

title: Agent makes many exploratory calls: what is it missing?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Agent calls tools just to learn what exists
Expose it as an MCP resource

title: Who needs the server, and how do they get it?
head: Situation
Right home
Why
rows: Whole team and CI need the server from a checkout
Version control shares it with every clone
Only one machine (e.g. the CI runner) uses it
Personal scope is enough; nothing to share
File is committed; the value is not
Keeps trials out of everyone's tool list
Standard integration such as an issue tracker
rule: If a tool must reach everyone who clones the repo, declare it in .mcp.json; put secrets in as ${VARS}, never as values.

title: Too many tool calls: what is the agent actually missing?
head: What you observe
What's missing
Fix
rows: Probing calls to learn what exists

One generic tool doing several jobs

Built-in Grep preferred over a better MCP tool
rule: Exploratory calls to discover content → expose a catalog as an MCP resource. Wrong tool choice → fix descriptions.

title: A better tool is ignored: which lever comes first?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
